raw_case_text:
A 31-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital for the treatment of newly diagnosed drug-resistant (pre-extensively drug resistant) pulmonary tuberculosis (chest X-ray at time of diagnosis - Fig. 1). She was treated with second-line antituberculosis drugs: moxifloxacin, kanamycin, cycloserine, prothionamide, para-aminosalicylic acid. After 3 weeks of therapy she developed high fever (> 39 C), lymphadenopathy in the cervical and axillary regions and pruritic maculopapular eruption all over the body (Fig. 2). Hematologic abnormalities such as leukocytosis with eosinophilia (1.81 x 109/l) and monocytosis (1.85 x 109/l) were detected in peripheral blood of the patient. Hepatitis was asymptomatic and detected by the evaluation of liver function: serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 1379 IU/l and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 1221 IU/l; levels of liver enzymes were increased by approximately 30-40-fold above the normal limits. The positive diagnosis of Epstein-Barr infection was based on the onset of increase in the anti-Epstein-Barr immunoglobulin (Ig) G titer (> 200 U/ml), implicating Epstein-Barr virus re-activation. Based on the clinic and laboratory findings diagnosis of DiHS/DRESS was suspected, and all the drugs were discontinued. Symptoms and laboratory abnormalities gradually resolved over 4 weeks without additional treatment.
A patch test was performed and analyzed according to the recommendations. The results of the patch test are presented in Table 1 and Figure 3. Treatment was adjusted to ethambutol, kanamycin, cycloserine, pyrazinamide, and linezolid, and no new symptoms were observed.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old woman presented with high fever (>39 °C), generalized pruritic maculopapular rash, and lymphadenopathy three weeks after starting second-line antituberculosis medications.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 31-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital and commenced on second-line antituberculosis medications. After 3 weeks of therapy, she acutely developed high-grade fever (>39 °C), bilateral cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy, and a generalized pruritic maculopapular eruption. All second-line drugs were discontinued upon suspicion of a severe adverse drug reaction, with gradual symptom resolution over 4 weeks without additional systemic therapy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Pre-extensively drug-resistant (pre-XDR) pulmonary tuberculosis. Prior hospitalizations, non-TB medical conditions, travel, or epidemiological exposures not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports high fever, generalized pruritic eruption, cervical and axillary swelling; denies abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or acute dyspnea outside baseline. Home medications: moxifloxacin, kanamycin, cycloserine, prothionamide, para-aminosalicylic acid. Allergies not documented prior to reaction.

objective.physical_examination: Body temperature >39 °C. Dermatologic: generalized pruritic maculopapular eruption covering the entire body. Lymphatic: palpable lymphadenopathy in cervical and axillary regions. Abdomen: soft, non-tender, no overt jaundice on physical inspection.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC: leukocytosis with eosinophilia (1.81 x 10^9/L) and monocytosis (1.85 x 10^9/L); liver function tests: serum AST 1,379 IU/L, serum ALT 1,221 IU/L (transaminases elevated 30-40-fold above upper normal limit); Chest X-ray: baseline pulmonary infiltrates at time of diagnosis.
objective.advanced_workup: Anti-Epstein-Barr virus IgG titer: markedly increased (>200 U/mL), indicating EBV reactivation. Drug patch testing performed according to international guidelines.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Drug-induced Hypersensitivity Syndrome / Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DiHS/DRESS) with severe acute hepatitis and Epstein-Barr virus reactivation, secondary to second-line antituberculosis agents, in a patient with pre-extensively drug-resistant (pre-XDR) pulmonary tuberculosis.
Confirmation: Clinical triad of high fever (>39 °C), generalized rash, peripheral lymphadenopathy, marked peripheral eosinophilia (1.81 x 10^9/L) and monocytosis (1.85 x 10^9/L), 30-40-fold transaminitis (AST 1,379 IU/L, ALT 1,221 IU/L), rising anti-EBV IgG titers (>200 U/mL) demonstrating viral reactivation, and positive drug patch testing.
Differentials ruled out: Acute viral hepatitis (A, B, C) and primary EBV mononucleosis.
Treatment & Outcome: Immediate cessation of all second-line antituberculosis medications. Clinical symptoms and laboratory abnormalities completely resolved over 4 weeks without corticosteroids. Antituberculosis treatment was successfully adjusted to ethambutol, kanamycin, cycloserine, pyrazinamide, and linezolid, with no recurrence of adverse reactions.
